newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DRIVER GOAL IN FINAL MINUTE GIVES RANGERS WIN OVER DUCKS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-DRIVER GOAL IN FINAL MINUTE GIVES RANGERS WIN OVER DUCKS.

text.p: Bruce Driver's power-play goal with 17.3 seconds to go -- the Rangers' third of the game with the man advantage -- lifted New York to a 3-2 win over the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim Friday, its sixth win in seven games.
Anaheim defenceman Darren Van Impe was penalised for interference with 1:53 left in the third period, giving the league's best power play its fifth chance of the game.
A slap shot from the left point by Brian Leetch never reached the net and the puck caromed to the top of the right faceoff circle, where Driver fired a slap shot over goaltender Guy Hebert's glove.
It was just Driver's second goal of the season, and survived a video replay to determine if teammate Adam Graves was in the crease.
"I knew Adam was in front. I didn't know if he was in the crease of if he got his stick on it. I just kept my fingers crossed," Driver said.

"I think it was a really bad call," said Anaheim coach Ron Wilson. "It's a 2-2 game and we get an interference call. I thought (Graves) was in the crease. As soon as the goal went in, I looked at (referee Kerry) Fraser and pointed right away."
Leetch had a pair of assists and became the highest-scoring defenceman in Ranger history with 612 points. New York was 3-for-5 on the power play, improving to 26.2 percent for the season.
Mike Richter made 28 saves for the Rangers, extending his personal unbeaten streak to 12 games (11-0-1).
Hebert was stellar for the Ducks, turning aside 45 shots.
"Last night was one of the worst games we played this year," said New York's Wayne Gretzky, referring to a 5-2 loss at Ottawa.

"But tonight, we regrouped. Richter was on his game and we worked hard for this win. Our power play has been pretty consistent all year and Brian was obviously the catalyst tonight on the power play."

In Phoenix, Deron Quint's second goal of the game, a power-play tally one minute into the third period, snapped a tie and sparked a four-goal outburst as the Coyotes erupted for a 7-4 victory over the slumping Vancouver Canucks.

Keith Tkachuk, Jim Johnson, Mike Gartner, Jeremy Roenick and Cliff Ronning also scored for the Coyotes, who notched a season-high seven goals and have won six of their last eight games. Phoenix is 11-0-1 when scoring four or more goals.
Quint, who entered with just one goal in 14 games, snapped a 3-3 tie when his wrist shot was stopped by goaltender Kirk McLean, who kicked the rebound off teammate Dana Murzyn into the net.
Gartner followed with a goal 81 seconds later and Roenick made it 6-3 with 13:10 remaining before Ronning capped the outburst with a power-play marker at 16:49.
McLean was rusty in his first start since November 11, allowing seven goals on 26 shots. He was activated Thursday after missing 18 games with a knee injury.
Vancouver has lost three straight and has been outscored 20-5 in the process. The Canucks have dropped seven of their last nine games, allowing 35 goals in that span.

In St Louis, Felix Potvin made 35 saves, including 18 in the second period, and Doug Gilmour and Todd Warriner scored power-play goals, leading the Toronto Maple Leafs to a 3-2 victory over the slumping Blues.
Jamie Baker also scored and Larry Murphy had two assists for the Maple Leafs, who have won three of four meetings with the Blues this season.
The Blues fell to 1-6-2 in their last nine games. St Louis is 1-3-1 since Jimmy Roberts took over as head coach for the fired Mike Keenan.

The crowd of 20,100 on Brett Hull tribute night was the Blues' largest of the season. Hull was honoured in pre-game ceremonies for scoring his 500th career goal. But the St Louis star was held pointless on seven shots on goal.
At Dallas, Mike Modano and Dave Reid each had a goal and two assists as the Stars defeated the Boston Bruins 6-4, ending their four-game unbeaten streak.
Ex-Bruin Andy Moog turned aside 17 shots for the Stars, who lead the Western Conference with 22 wins.
Jozef Stumpel had a goal and Ray Bourque added three assists for Boston.
In Edmonton, John LeClair scored a pair of second-period goals and added an assist as the Philadelphia Flyers extended their unbeaten streak to 12 games with a 6-4 win over the Oilers.
Paul Coffey and Danius Zubrus each added a goal and an assist as the Flyers improved to 10-0-2 since November 27. They have outscored opponents 49-22 during the streak.
Philadelphia broke a 13-game winless streak in Edmonton, winning there for the first time since January 2, 1985.
